newsitem.title: UK: BA slips as U.S. halts "open skies" talks.
newsitem.headline: BA slips as U.S. halts "open skies" talks.

text.p: Shares in British Airways fell on Tuesday after the U.S. said it had called off aviation talks with Britain planned for later this week.
The shares were 2-1/2p lower at 527-1/2p by 1411 GMT after trading around 530p just before the announcement.
The U.S. Transportation Department has said that an "open skies' agreement was needed before anti-trust immunity could be given to the proposed alliance between British Airways and American Airlines.
Talks between the two countries were scheduled to start on Wednesday.

"The UK proposal that was provided fell so far short of providing the essential elements of an open skies agreement, it did not provide the basis for discussion," a U.S. transport department spokesman said.
"It was never going to easy for the two sides to reach common ground," said one leading aviation analyst who declined to be named.
"I have always been rather sceptical how after 18 years they suddenly think all the problems will be solved within three months,"he added.
"This highlights how much the U.S. wants out of these negotiations and how little the UK is prepared to concede."
